headline: BNP MP Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti resigns, seat declared vacant
summary: The reserved seat MP resigned following a directive from the Prime Minister over allegations regarding the Radda centre attack.
details: BNP reserved-seat Member of Parliament Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti has resigned from her position, and the Speaker of the National Parliament has officially declared her seat vacant.
The resignation comes after the Prime Minister directed her to step down from the parliament following allegations and calls for her resignation over an attack on the Radda centre.
Prior to the resignation, Mishti met with the Speaker of the National Parliament, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, to discuss the matter.
Speaking to the media, she stated that she will abide by whatever the BNP decides regarding her resignation.
The vacancy of the reserved seat for women is now official, following the acceptance of the resignation letter by the Speaker.
caption:
BNP MP Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti has resigned from parliament following a directive from the Prime Minister.

BNP reserved-seat Member of Parliament Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti has resigned from her position, and the Speaker of the National Parliament has officially declared her seat vacant.

The resignation comes after the Prime Minister directed her to step down from the parliament following allegations and calls for her resignation over an attack on the Radda centre.

Prior to the resignation, Mishti met with the Speaker of the National Parliament, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, to discuss the matter.

Speaking to the media, she stated that she will abide by whatever the BNP decides regarding her resignation.

The vacancy of the reserved seat for women is now official, following the acceptance of the resignation letter by the Speaker.

#Bangladesh #Politics #BNP #Parliament #News

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com, The Daily Star

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman: [[Some parties trying to create anarchy]] by exploiting incidents
headline: PM Tarique Rahman: Some parties trying to create anarchy by exploiting incidents
summary: The Prime Minister warned that certain political groups are attempting to spark chaos in the country, while urging a 'secret group' to address internal abuse cases first.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that some political parties are attempting to create anarchy in Bangladesh by exploiting untoward incidents. He made these remarks during a rally at the 'Muhuri-Kahua Flood Control' project inauguration in Feni's Parshuram.

The Prime Minister referred to a 'secret group' that has been offering advice to the government, claiming that members of this group are involved in the abuses of women. He urged them to 'look at their own house first' and handle their internal issues before advising others.

Tarique Rahman further alleged that certain members of this group are under investigation for abusing women, and mentioned a claim that one of their leaders had caused a person's death through torture.
Addressing the opposition, he claimed that some parties had won seats in the February 12 election by misleading people and are now plotting to create chaos in the country.
He also reminded the audience of the role of these parties in 1971, citing their history of violence against women and claiming they have once again chosen the path of anarchy and abuse.

Regarding the the flood control project, the Prime Minister noted that a major flood occurred two to two-and-a-half years ago where water flowed over the bridge. This project is part of the government's election promise to prevent such disasters.
